note: Kolkata has no single restoration register. Entries are compiled from named, dated sources and graded V (verified against a primary source or our own ingested data), N (news-sourced) or C (claimed). Water quality for both Sarobars comes from our own WBPCB ingest, so this page and the rivers page read the same samples.

bodies.name: Rabindra Sarobar
bodies.era: Excavated by the Calcutta Improvement Trust in the early 1920s
bodies.builder: Calcutta Improvement Trust - its first chairman Cecil Henry Bompass, KMC chief engineer M.R. Atkins, and Prabodh Chandra Chatterjee of Shibpur B.E. College
bodies.feed: Rainwater and groundwater; no natural inflow, which is why silt accumulates rather than flushes
bodies.status: 192 acres in total, of which about 73 are open water and the rest mature planting, some of it over a century old. The NGT appointed KMDA custodian in 2017; KMDA has since sought fresh NGT permission to dredge, the lake having gone without proper desilting for two to three decades. WBPCB's own sampling on 2026-07-02 recorded dissolved oxygen 8.0 mg/l, BOD 2.9 mg/l and faecal coliform 220 MPN/100ml - by some distance the cleanest water we hold for Rabindra Sarobar's city.
bodies.cultural_note: Renamed from Dhakuria Lake in May 1958 in tribute to Rabindranath Tagore, and included in the Ministry of Environment and Forests' National Lake Conservation Plan. Recorded bird species have fallen from 118 in 2021 to 110 through October 2023 as pollution has risen - the clearest ecological series the city has for any water body.

bodies.name: Subhas Sarobar
bodies.era: Developed in the 1950s from a natural depression
bodies.builder: Post-independence state development; maintained by KMDA
bodies.status: About 73 acres including the surrounding parkland. Suffers encroachment and irregular maintenance; desilting, aeration and community programmes have been run at various points. WBPCB's own sampling on 2026-06-04 recorded dissolved oxygen 8.9 mg/l, BOD 3.6 mg/l and faecal coliform 450 MPN/100ml - by some distance the cleanest water we hold for Subhas Sarobar's city.
bodies.cultural_note: The eastern counterpart to Rabindra Sarobar, and the second of the two lakes the NGT's Chhath Puja restrictions were sought for.

bodies.name: Lal Dighi
bodies.era: Pre-colonial; the tank the colonial settlement was laid out around
bodies.builder: Pre-dates the British settlement; adopted as the centrepiece of Dalhousie Square
bodies.status: Survives at the centre of B.B.D. Bagh, ringed by the city's colonial administrative core - one of the few central Kolkata tanks never filled.
bodies.cultural_note: The city of Kolkata was laid out around this pond; the British called it the Great Tank. That a city organised itself around a pond, and then filled roughly 44% of its ponds within two decades, is the whole of Kolkata's water history in one object.

bodies.name: East Kolkata Wetlands
bodies.era: Evolved from the early twentieth century as the Bidyadhari silted up
bodies.builder: Not built - a fishery system that grew around the city's sewage outfall
bodies.feed: Kolkata's raw sewage, carried east through the dry-weather flow channels
bodies.status: 12,500 hectares holding 254 sewage-fed fisheries across 37 mouzas, treating 910 MLD - 65% of Kolkata's sewage, roughly five times what all five of the city's treatment plants manage combined. Protected under the East Kolkata Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Act 2006, and under continuous real-estate pressure; EKWMA publishes FIR and charge-sheet records against encroachment.
bodies.cultural_note: A Ramsar site, and the only case on this platform where a city's largest piece of water infrastructure is neither built, owned, nor paid for by the city - and lies outside its boundary.
